finding: Whitespace membership is exactly Rust char.is_whitespace over Unicode scalar input.
limit: CeTTa's byte-oriented C isspace and Lean's narrower Char.isWhitespace paths must converge on the generated scalar-aware relation.

finding: A quote is permitted after the first scalar of a word.
limit: CeTTa and LeaTTa currently dispatch every quote as a string delimiter rather than only dispatching string at token start.

finding: A quote is permitted in a variable name after dollar.
limit: The generated reader must preserve the written variable production.

finding: Hash is reserved and excluded from variable names.
limit: LeaTTa's declarative reserveHashInVariable field is currently not consumed by its parser; exact diagnostic wording is separate from rejection parity.

finding: VARIABLE requires a following scalar while WORD admits dollar through CHAR; the written alternatives do not state ordered-choice resolution.
limit: Rust and the current GSLT construct an empty-name variable; CeTTa constructs a dollar symbol; LeaTTa constructs a free variable whose spelling is dollar.

finding: Semicolon is excluded from VARIABLE because it is excluded from CHAR and is not added explicitly.
limit: The current GSLT follows Rust here and must be corrected before production routing.

finding: A comment stops before either carriage return or line feed.
limit: All executable readers currently stop comments only at line feed; the ratified LanguageDef must follow the written EOL production unless the specification is amended.

finding: Top-level bang is program syntax selecting evaluation of the following atom, except for the documented bang-leading-symbol ambiguity.
limit: The generated reader must compose the atom grammar with a versioned program-form layer before it replaces CeTTa's full file reader.

finding: Bang-leading symbol behavior is documented as an implementation artifact and not a strong requirement.
limit: LeaTTa already exposes compatibility and canonical policies; the production LanguageDef must select the intended profile explicitly.

finding: The written STRING production does not enumerate escapes, while API prose refers to non-escaped quotes.
limit: Ratify whether backslash introduces an escape and which source spellings are legal.

finding: The simple escape repertoire and decoded values are not specified.
limit: Rust decodes a closed repertoire; CeTTa accepts every following byte and removes the backslash; LeaTTa preserves the quoted source token.

finding: The backslash-x byte escape is not specified.
limit: Current Rust and GSLT use exactly two hex digits and restrict the result to ASCII; CeTTa leaves x and both digits literal; LeaTTa preserves the source token.

finding: The backslash-u Unicode escape body is not specified.
limit: Choose brace discipline and digit bounds explicitly; do not inherit Rust's empty-body, extra-open-brace, or eight-digit acceptance accidentally.

finding: The handling of an unknown backslash escape is not specified.
limit: Rust constructs an incomplete error node; CeTTa drops the backslash; LeaTTa accepts and preserves the source spelling.

finding: WORD and STRING may be converted to grounded atoms by an ordered runtime tokenizer environment.
limit: The empty-tokenizer canonical syntax lane and LeaTTa Pattern parser are not by themselves the production HE Atom reader; tokenizer actions need a separately versioned compilation input.

finding: Recovery trees, ranges, and diagnostic text are not specified by the grammar.
limit: Valid-source recognition and comparable rejection positions precede any claim of recovery-tree parity.
